drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. 68-year-old male admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.66, creatinine 0.88-1.03, hemoglobin 13.4-13.5, platelets 224-228, sodium 139, wbc 6.6; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 80-84, map 92-96, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 125-131, spo2 97-98, temp 36.5-36.7
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.26-1.43, hemoglobin 13.4-13.6, platelets 228-229, sodium 139, wbc 6.4-6.7; vitals dbp 76-80, heart_rate 80-85, map 92-95, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-17, sbp 123-127, spo2 97-98, temp 36.6-36.8
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Hold lisinopril; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 68-year-old male, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Type 2 diabetes. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient seen and examined at bedside.
